```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
require(tidyverse)

ESTIMAND_LEVELS <- c("stu", "dstu", .clu", ".clu")
ESTIMATOR_LEVELS <- c("LR w/ CRSE", "LR (agg, wt)", "DB_indiv (FE)", "DB_indiv (int)",
                      "LR (agg)", "DB_clust (int)", "DB_clust (FE)",
                      "MLM")
MAIN_ESTIMATORS <- c("LR w/ CRSE", "LR (agg)", "MLM")

COR_COLS <- c("size.impact.cor.block", "size.intercept.cor.block",
              "size.impact.cor.cluster", "proptx.impact.cor.block")
```

## Overview

This note covers the second set of simulations.
These include two different scenarios:

1. Simulation with block intercepts correlated with block sizes

    * Hypothesis: CRSE is biased?

2. Simulation with only 4 blocks and 6 clusters per block on average

    * Hypothesis: if there are very few blocks, CRSE should blow it
    
We're also using $\bar{p}=0.75$ instead of 0.5 to avoid "nice" cancellations.

    * Hypothesis: if there is correlation with block-level impact, CRSE should be biased
    * Since $p_j(1-p_j)$ weights can be quite low/high for particular clusters

TODO: in blkvar, implement correlations between site-level intercepts and site sizes?



Recall key for estimand names. 
We'll focus more on the first two, since none of our estimators target the second two:

* "stu": student-weighted
* .clu": cluster-weighted
* ("dstu": block-weighted student-weighted)
* (".clu": block-weighted cluster-weighted)

Recall also the three representative methods:

1. LR with CRSE (will also use DB_indiv to compare)
2. LR (agg)
3. MLM

## Simulation 1: correlation between block-level intercepts and sizes

```{r}
load( "results/aggregated_simulation_results_interceptcor.RData" )
# load( "results/aggregated_simulation_results_small.RData" )
```

### Overview of results

Absolute bias behaves roughly as expected, though weird results for dstu still (student-weighted estimators not much better than cluster-weighted).

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  group_by(method) %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("bias"), ~mean(abs(.)))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("bias")) %>%
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"),
                           levels = ESTIMAND_LEVELS),
         method = factor(method, levels = ESTIMATOR_LEVELS)) %>% 
  filter(finite) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid( ~ estimand) +
  coord_flip()  
```

RMSE is basically same as before, but still student-weighted methods are strictly dominated by cluster-weighted methods??

```{r}
RMSE.table

sruns %>% 
  group_by(method) %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("RMSE"), ~mean(abs(.)))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("RMSE")) %>%
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"),
                           levels = ESTIMAND_LEVELS),
         method = factor(method, levels = ESTIMATOR_LEVELS)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(finite ~ estimand) +
  coord_flip()
```

We see larger standard errors for the student-weighted methods.

```{r}
SE.table 

sruns %>% 
  group_by(method) %>% 
  summarize(across(starts_with("SE."), ~mean(.)), 
            mean.SE.hat = mean(mean.SE.hat)) %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("SE")) %>%
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = ESTIMATOR_LEVELS)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value, group=name, fill=name)) +
  geom_col(position="dodge") +
  coord_flip()
```

Coverage is all still generally sub-nominal.
DB_indiv (int) is particularly bad.

```{r}
sruns %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("cover")) %>% 
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"),
                           levels = ESTIMAND_LEVELS),
         method = factor(method, levels = ESTIMATOR_LEVELS)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(finite ~ estimand) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0.95),
             lty="dashed", color="red") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0.8, 1))
```

### Faceting by simulation setting

The simulation settings are below.
Note that I messed up some recording in the run, so I've manually fixed things.

```{r}
size.intercept.table <- tibble(
  ID = 1:16,
  size.intercept.cor.block = c(rep(0, 8), rep(0.8, 8))
)
sruns2 <- sruns %>% 
  left_join(size.intercept.table, by="ID") %>% 
  relocate(size.intercept.cor.block, .after=size.impact.cor.block)

# sruns2 %>% 
#   group_by(across(all_of(c("ID", COR_COLS)))) %>% 
#   summarize(n = n())
```

Absolute bias behaves roughly as expected, though weird results for dstu still (student-weighted estimators not much better than cluster-weighted).

```{r}
# all 2^4 settings
sruns2 %>% 
  select(ID, method, COR_COLS, starts_with("bias")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("bias")) %>% 
  mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
         estimand = factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"),
                           levels = ESTIMAND_LEVELS),
         method = factor(method, levels = ESTIMATOR_LEVELS)) %>% 
  filter(finite, estimand == "stu")
  
  # TODO: a bunch of marginal plots?
  #  - or a big colored table?

marginal_plot <- function(i1, i2, est) {
  sruns2 %>% 
    group_by(across(all_of(c("method", COR_COLS[c(i1,i2)])))) %>% 
    summarize(across(starts_with("bias"), ~mean(abs(.)))) %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
    pivot_longer(starts_with("bias")) %>%
    mutate(finite = str_detect(name, ".f"),
           estimand = factor(str_extract(name, "([^.]+$)"),
                             levels = ESTIMAND_LEVELS),
           method = factor(method, levels = ESTIMATOR_LEVELS)) %>% 
    filter(finite, estimand == est) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=method, y=value)) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_grid(reformulate(COR_COLS[i1], COR_COLS[i2]),
               labeller = label_both) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = paste("Average absolute bias"),
         subtitle = paste("Estimand:", est))
}
```

We know that: size.impact.cor makes a difference

Checking if proptx has any effect now: some effects

```{r}
COR_COLS
marginal_plot(2,4, "stu")
marginal_plot(2,4, .clu")

# marginal_plot(2,4, "dstu")
# marginal_plot(2,4, ".clu")

# other side
marginal_plot(1,3, "stu")
marginal_plot(1,3, .clu")

```




## Takeaways

1. DB_clust (int) and DB_indiv (int) seem to do much better in some settings? Need to dig here. In particular, it's now different from LR w/ CRSE, whereas it was the same before.

2. MLM generally does better than everything else in small sample sizes
